item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract. It adds the narrowly scoped replayable Upload API using the established multipart helper, while A introduces a prohibited SDK-wide request-body buffering and retry behavior change.","reasons":["B preserves existing Add behavior and avoids modifying shared request/retry machinery; A changes RawClient.Do for every io.Reader and explicitly changes Add and Update semantics, contrary to the contract’s scope restrictions.","Both candidates incorrectly duplicate Add’s request, option, decoding, and error logic instead of routing Upload through s.Add, but this defect is localized and easier to correct in B.","B’s retry test verifies the multipart payload is intact on both attempts, directly exercising replayability. A’s Upload retry test only counts attempts and discards each body, relying on separate broad RawClient/Add tests.","Both use internal/multipartbody.NewFile, provide the exact requested API, validate filename/content before a request, and preserve FilesOption handling in practical terms."],"risks_a":["The RawClient.Do change buffers arbitrary reader bodies whenever WithNoRetry is absent, even when the configured policy would not retry that request, causing potentially large memory use and changing streaming and source-read timing SDK-wide.","It alters Add and Update behavior and adds unrelated documentation and tests despite an explicit instruction not to refactor request/retry machinery.","Upload does not call FilesService.Add, duplicating its implementation and creating future divergence risk."],"risks_b":["Upload does not call FilesService.Add, violating the explicit single-path requirement and duplicating response/error handling.","It lacks the required source-reader failure test, although NewFile errors are visibly propagated.","Its Add documentation is unusually implementation-specific and could become stale; the claim that retries silently do not happen may also be better documented at the retry layer."]}
